sourceLine: your Škoda, Bentley and Sparta work, and the questions brands ask before they commission an experience

cards.title: Vision Pro Showrooms: What Škoda Teaches
cards.angle: Vision Pro has reportedly sold about 600,000 units in total, and a lighter successor is not expected before late 2028. A premium brand can still justify it when the headset serves a small, high-intent audience.
cards.evidence: Your Škoda Elroq and Epiq experience offers VR exploration or life-size mixed reality placement. Your Bentley app adds a haptic panel with real material samples and 3600 x 3200 per eye video. No audience numbers are published. Your Sept 4, 2026 configurator cost guide exists, so keep this on Vision Pro, not web configurators.

cards.title: AI Try-On Mirrors: Disclose the AI
cards.angle: The EU AI Act's Article 50 has applied since Aug 2, 2026, requiring disclosure when people interact with AI, with fines up to €15 million or 3% of turnover. AI-generated try-on images also need marking, with a Dec 2, 2026 grace period for systems already live.
cards.evidence: Your Sparta AI Mirror with Footballmania, ČSOB and Mastercard lets account holders try on merchandise through AI-generated images. It has an interactive quiz and QR sharing. No sales lift is published, and you are Prague-based, so EU rules apply directly.

cards.title: Luxury XR After Vision Pro: Design to Port
cards.angle: Meta announced VR Glasses on Sept 23, 2026 at $1,300 for spring 2027, while Apple's lighter successor is not expected before late 2028. Luxury brands should build experience logic that moves across headsets.
cards.evidence: Your Škoda, Bentley and ASAHI projects are all Vision Pro builds, and Bentley blends image target recognition with life-size configuration. The article asks which pieces are device-specific and which would port.
